questions.q: What is the final output of this algorithm?
questions.code:
x = 1
WHILE x < 20
    x = x * 2
ENDWHILE
OUTPUT x
questions.explain: x goes 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32; the loop stops when x is 32.

questions.q: A binary search is generally faster than a linear search on a large sorted list.
Validation checks that the data entered is correct and true.
questions.explain: Validation only checks that data is reasonable (e.g. within a range); it cannot check that it is true.

questions.q: A bubble sort compares items that are next to each other.
A nested loop is a loop inside another loop.
A ____ search repeatedly halves the list to find an item.
Checking that data is sensible, such as an age between 0 and 120, is called ____.
Following an algorithm with test data and writing the values in a table is called a ____ table.
The ____ sort repeatedly swaps neighbouring items that are in the wrong order.
Write pseudocode to input 5 numbers and output their total.
questions.answer: total = 0 (1); loop 5 times with INPUT and total = total + number (1); OUTPUT total after the loop (1).

questions.q: Explain why a binary search is more efficient than a linear search on a large sorted list.
questions.answer: A binary search halves the number of items to check each time (1); a linear search may have to check every item (1).

questions.q: Describe what validation is and give one example.
questions.answer: Validation checks that data entered is sensible/allowed (1); example: range check, length check, presence check or type check (1).
